title: 410. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Finding Missing Right-Triangle Sides
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Opposite side from hypotenuse and angle
questions.learningObjective: Find the side opposite a given acute angle from the hypotenuse using sine.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is \(10\text{ cm}\) and one acute angle is \(30^\circ\). What is the length of the side opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle?
questions.explanation: Since \(\sin 30^\circ=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\), the opposite side is \(10\sin 30^\circ=10\cdot\frac{1}{2}=5\text{ cm}\). The value \(5\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\) is \(10\cos 30^\circ\), the side adjacent to the angle.
questions.hint: Choose the ratio that links the opposite side and the hypotenuse.

questions.concept: Hypotenuse from adjacent side and angle
questions.learningObjective: Find the hypotenuse from the side adjacent to a given acute angle using cosine.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side adjacent to a \(60^\circ\) angle is \(8\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Since \(\cos 60^\circ=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\), the hypotenuse is \(\frac{8}{\cos 60^\circ}=\frac{8}{1/2}=16\text{ cm}\). Multiplying \(8\) by \(\cos 60^\circ\) gives \(4\text{ cm}\), which is shorter than a leg and so cannot be the hypotenuse.
questions.hint: Write the cosine ratio and solve for the hypotenuse; the hypotenuse must be the longest side.

questions.concept: Adjacent side from opposite side and angle
questions.learningObjective: Find a leg from the other leg and an acute angle using tangent.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite a \(45^\circ\) angle is \(6\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the side adjacent to that angle?
questions.explanation: Since \(\tan 45^\circ=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=1\), the adjacent side equals the opposite side, \(6\text{ cm}\). The value \(6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\) is the hypotenuse of this triangle.
questions.hint: The two legs are linked by the tangent of the angle.

questions.concept: Adjacent side from hypotenuse and angle
questions.learningObjective: Find the side adjacent to a given acute angle from the hypotenuse using cosine.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is \(12\text{ cm}\) and one acute angle is \(60^\circ\). What is the length of the side adjacent to the \(60^\circ\) angle?
questions.explanation: The adjacent side is \(12\cos 60^\circ=12\cdot\frac{1}{2}=6\text{ cm}\). The value \(6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\) is \(12\sin 60^\circ\), the side opposite the angle.
questions.hint: The adjacent side and the hypotenuse are linked by cosine.

questions.concept: Opposite side from adjacent side and angle
questions.learningObjective: Find the side opposite a given acute angle from the adjacent side using tangent.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side adjacent to a \(60^\circ\) angle is \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the side opposite that angle?
questions.explanation: Since \(\tan 60^\circ=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\), the opposite side is \(5\tan 60^\circ=5\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\). Dividing by \(\tan 60^\circ\) instead gives \(\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ cm}\), which is incorrect.
questions.hint: Write the tangent ratio and solve for the opposite side.

questions.learningObjective: Model a ladder against a wall with a right triangle and find a missing side.
questions.question: A ladder \(6\text{ m}\) long leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the horizontal ground. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse, and the height is the side opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle. Hence the height is \(6\sin 60^\circ=6\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=3\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\approx 5.2\text{ m}\). The value \(3\text{ m}=6\cos 60^\circ\) is the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall.
questions.hint: Identify the hypotenuse, then decide whether the height is opposite or adjacent to the given angle.

questions.concept: Missing side with a non-standard angle
questions.learningObjective: Use given decimal values of sine and cosine to find a side.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is \(20\text{ cm}\) and one acute angle is \(35^\circ\). Using \(\sin 35^\circ\approx 0.574\) and \(\cos 35^\circ\approx 0.819\), what is the length of the side opposite the \(35^\circ\) angle, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The opposite side is \(20\sin 35^\circ\approx 20\cdot 0.574=11.48\approx 11.5\text{ cm}\). The value \(16.4\text{ cm}\approx 20\cdot 0.819\) is the adjacent side.
questions.hint: Decide which of the two given ratios involves the opposite side.

questions.learningObjective: Set up the trigonometric equation that gives an unknown side.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side adjacent to a \(40^\circ\) angle is \(9\text{ cm}\), and \(x\) is the side opposite that angle. Which equation gives \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The two legs are related by \(\tan 40^\circ=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{x}{9}\). Multiplying both sides by \(9\) gives \(x=9\tan 40^\circ\). The expression \(\frac{9}{\tan 40^\circ}\) would be correct only if \(9\text{ cm}\) were the opposite side.
questions.hint: Write the tangent ratio with \(x\) in the numerator, then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Height from an angle of elevation
questions.learningObjective: Use an angle of elevation and a horizontal distance to find a height.
questions.question: From a point on level ground \(60\text{ m}\) from the base of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of the top is \(30^\circ\). How tall is the tower?
questions.explanation: The height is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle and the \(60\text{ m}\) distance is adjacent to it. Hence the height is \(60\tan 30^\circ=60\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=20\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\approx 34.6\text{ m}\). Using \(\tan 60^\circ=\sqrt{3}\) instead gives \(60\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\), which is incorrect.
questions.hint: The horizontal distance and the height are the two legs; use the tangent of the angle of elevation.

questions.concept: Perimeter from one side and one angle
questions.learningObjective: Find both missing sides of a right triangle and combine them.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite a \(30^\circ\) angle is \(4\text{ cm}\). What is the perimeter of the triangle?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is \(\frac{4}{\sin 30^\circ}=8\text{ cm}\). The adjacent side is \(\frac{4}{\tan 30^\circ}=4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\). The perimeter is \(4+8+4\sqrt{3}=12+4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\). Multiplying by \(\tan 30^\circ\) instead of dividing gives the incorrect adjacent side \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Find the hypotenuse with sine and the other leg with tangent, then add the three sides.
